report:
Finding: The evidence supports a domain/genre shift: Model B (relative to A) has a stronger residual-stream feature that points toward food/restaurant/lifestyle/blogging vocabulary, concentrated at the earliest token positions and propagated through middle→late layers. In other words, B is biased toward “restaurant/cooking/food-blog” style continuations early in the context.

Why I conclude this
- L2-norm pattern: the difference is concentrated at pos0/pos1 across many later layers (very large spikes at layers 16–25, especially pos0 and pos1). That means the models differ mainly in how they represent the first one or two tokens and that the difference is amplified through deeper layers.
- Logit-lens signals: the high‑norm cells consistently decode to tokens from a coherent topic cluster: “restaurant”, “Restaurant”, “cooking”, “Cook”, “Chef”, “baking”, “Cake”, “blogs”, “blogger(s)”, “restaurant(s)”, “Cafe”, “kitchen”, “cooked”, “professional” and related words appear repeatedly across layers and positions. These tokens appear at many of the top cells (especially pos2–pos4 and pos1 in later layers), indicating a systematic tilt in vocabulary space.
- Secondary support: other repeated tokens (e.g., “metropolitan”, “dissertation”, “chiropractic”, “billionaire”, “polyurethane”) suggest the shift isn’t a single narrow keyword but a style/genre mix typical of local commerce/lifestyle/consumer web content (restaurant pieces, reviews, lifestyle blogs, small-business copy).

Caveats
- The signal isn’t purely food-only; other commercial/local/lifestyle tokens appear, so the difference could be a broader tilt toward commercial/lifestyle/web-content domains rather than strictly recipes.
- Patchscope readouts were not provided in the prompt, so I can’t show actual sampled continuations; the conclusion rests on the logit-lens decodes + where the L2 mass sits.
- I cannot (and do not) claim a specific training objective or exact fine-tuning dataset; I name the interpretable difference as a domain/topic bias because the decoded tokens repeatedly point that way.

If you want, I can (a) try to reconstruct likely continuations by injecting the difference into identity prompts (if you can provide patchscope outputs), or (b) produce targeted logit-lens analyses for additional positions/layers to refine whether the bias is primarily “food/recipes” vs. “local-business/lifestyle.”
